snapshot.title: TNPSC Polity: Constitutional & Non-Constitutional Bodies
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Polity Hook: 324: Election. 148: CAG. 315: PSC. 1929: TNPSC. 280: FC. 6 yr/65: CAG term.

quick_notes.title: Election Commission (Art 324)
quick_notes.detail: Free and fair elections. Conducts LS, RS, State Assembly, President, VP elections.
quick_notes.explanation: The Election Commission is a permanent body created by Article 324 of the Indian Constitution to make sure elections are free and fair, meaning no voter is forced or cheated. This Article gives the Commission the power to supervise, direct, and control all elections in the country. The Commission conducts elections for the Lok Sabha (the lower house of Parliament), the Rajya Sabha (the upper house of Parliament), each State Legislative Assembly, the President of India, and the Vice President of India.

quick_notes.title: UPSC & TNPSC (Art 315)
quick_notes.detail: Recruitment for All India and State services. TNPSC was the first provincial PSC in India (est. 1929).
quick_notes.explanation: The Union Public Service Commission, commonly called UPSC, is the central agency that recruits people for All India Services such as the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and for posts in the Union government. The Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission, or TNPSC, is the state-level agency that recruits people for government jobs within the state of Tamil Nadu. Article 315 of the Indian Constitution specifically provides for the creation of both a Union Public Service Commission and a separate Public Service Commission for each state. TNPSC holds the distinction of being the first provincial Public Service Commission in India, having been established in 1929, before India gained independence.

quick_notes.title: CAG (Art 148)
quick_notes.detail: Comptroller and Auditor General. Audits govt accounts. Appointed by President for 6 years or 65 age.
quick_notes.explanation: The Comptroller and Auditor General, or CAG, is India’s top auditor who checks how the government spends public money. Article 148 of the Constitution establishes this office and its rules. The President of India appoints the CAG, and the CAG serves for a term of either six years or until reaching age 65, whichever comes first. The CAG’s main job is to audit all government accounts, meaning to carefully examine the government’s financial records to ensure money is used correctly, legally, and efficiently. This helps keep the government honest about its spending.

quick_notes.title: Finance Commission (Art 280)
quick_notes.detail: Already covered in Economy; recap: tax distribution between Center and States.
quick_notes.explanation: Finance Commission (Article 280) The Finance Commission is a special body set up by the President of India every five years to decide how tax money collected by the central government should be shared with the state governments. Article 280 of the Indian Constitution says the President must create this commission to recommend the distribution of taxes between the Centre and the States. The commission also advises on grants-in-aid, which are extra funds given to states that need more financial help. Its members are appointed by the President and include a chairman and four other experts in finance or economics. The main goal is to ensure fair and balanced financial resources for all states, especially poorer ones. This helps maintain unity and reduce economic inequality across the country.

quick_notes.title: Non-Constitutional Bodies
quick_notes.detail: NITI Aayog, NHRC (Human Rights), CIC (Information), CVC (Vigilance), Lokpal & Lokayukta (Anti-corruption).
quick_notes.explanation: Non-Constitutional Bodies are organizations that are not created by the Indian Constitution itself, but are set up by laws passed by Parliament or by government orders. For example, NITI Aayog, which stands for the National Institution for Transforming India, was created by a government resolution in 2015 to replace the old Planning Commission and help plan economic policies. The National Human Rights Commission, or NHRC, was established by the Protection of Human Rights Act of 1993 to investigate complaints about violations of human rights. The Central Information Commission, or CIC, was set up under the Right to Information Act of 2005 to hear appeals from people who are denied information by government offices. The Central Vigilance Commission, or CVC, was created by a government resolution in 1964 and later given legal status by the Central Vigilance Commission Act of 2003 to fight corruption in government departments. Finally, the Lokpal is a national anti-corruption body for central government officials, and Lokayuktas are similar bodies for state governments, both established by the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act of 2013.

TNPSC was the first provincial PSC in India (est. 1929). CAG (Art 148): Comptroller and Auditor General. Audits govt accounts. Appointed by President for 6 years or 65 age. Finance Commission (Art 280): Already covered in Economy; recap: tax distribution between Center and States. Non-Constitutional Bodies: NITI Aayog, NHRC (Human Rights), CIC (Information), CVC (Vigilance), Lokpal & Lokayukta (Anti-corruption).
